steps.say: A ninety-nine million parameter model, first under two hundred and fifty million on a leaderboard, and fifty-six percent on an arithmetic test.

steps.caption: KLM 1.5 scored 48.20, KLM 1.6 scored 55.90
steps.say: The claim is that one change did it: a longer learning-rate decay.

scenes.headline: What KLM 1.6 is made of
scenes.sub: Counted from its header, checked against its benchmark
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Odile. I read this model's files and its benchmark. Here is what's inside.

states.say: Twenty-four layers, five hundred and twelve wide.

states.term: Hybrid: recurrent layers with a few attention layers
states.say: Every fourth is attention, which caches every token. The other eighteen are recurrent, with a fixed memory.

params.state: state S: key rows, value columns

steps.say: Here is that memory, as a toy head. A token writes a value at a key, and reading that key returns it.
A second key overlaps the first. Its write leaks through the shared channel.
Rewrite the first key with one gate for erase and write. The new value lands, but the second key drops to zero point eight seven.
Gated DeltaNet-2 gives erase and write their own gates. Erase everything, write at half strength. One gate cannot do that.
KLM's layer follows the paper's block closely. Each gate has its own projection and its own sigmoid.
steps.term: Gated DeltaNet-2: separate erase and write gates

scenes.title: Where the 99M parameters go, in %
scenes.say: Half the parameters are feed-forward. The embedding is two percent: the vocabulary is tiny, and numbers are split into digits.

scenes.credit: the article's plot of both cards

steps.say: Now the decay. KLM 1.5 took its learning rate to zero over twenty billion tokens. KLM 1.6 takes a hundred billion.

steps.caption: 100B vs 180B tokens, 128 vs 192 sequences per step
steps.say: That also means eighty billion more tokens, a bigger batch, and new math data. Not just the schedule.

states.say: The arithmetic test offers four consecutive whole numbers for every question.

states.term: Distractors: always the answer plus or minus one or two
states.say: In most, only the last digit differs. So the test mostly asks: which last digit?

scenes.credit: the article's plot of the leaderboard

steps.say: On that test, two models under two hundred and fifty million score higher, one of them smaller than KLM.

steps.caption: Third under 250M on ArithMark-3
steps.say: KLM 1.6 is third under two hundred and fifty million. Its first place on the index is less than one point.

scenes.text: A careful 99M base model. The decay was not the only change, and the lead rests on a last-digit test.
scenes.say: A careful small base model, with an honest card. But the decay was not the only change, and the lead rests on a last-digit test.

recap: ArithMark-3 is mostly the last digit
scenes.say: Recurrent layers with separate gates, a longer decay with more data, and a narrow test. Thanks for watching!
